guide.title: Your Guide to Preparing a Scholarship Application Package
guide.subtitle: A detailed, step-by-step practical roadmap to help you prepare and organize all required documents for international scholarships with the highest acceptance standards.

roadmap.title: The Standout Application Roadmap
roadmap.step1Desc: Carefully check eligibility criteria, minimum GPA, and language requirements before investing time in an application.
roadmap.step2Desc: Establish a timeline marking application closing dates and schedule document preparation at least one month in advance.
roadmap.step3Desc: Translate certified transcripts and degree certificates through authorized translators and keep clear high-res PDFs.
roadmap.step4Desc: Draft an original, concise personal statement explaining your academic journey, future goals, and reasons for choosing this specific program.
roadmap.step5Desc: Reach out to your professors or mentors 4-6 weeks in advance to allow ample time for personalized reference letters.
roadmap.step6Desc: Proofread your application, verify all required attachments are in place, and submit at least two days before the deadline.

docs.title: Core Documents for Most Opportunities
docs.doc1Desc: Chronological, focused on academic accomplishments, projects, and skills relevant to the opportunity.
docs.doc2Desc: Articulates your genuine interest, background, and alignment with the program goals.
docs.doc3Desc: From academic professors or professional managers who have directly supervised your performance.
docs.doc4Desc: Officially translated and notarized according to the host institution's requirements.
docs.passportDesc: Primary proof of identity and nationality. The source recommends at least 18 months of remaining validity at time of application to cover admissions review, visa issuance, and student residency.
docs.passportTip: Practical tip: Color scan data and signature pages in high resolution PDF format, verifying full English name spelling matches all other academic credentials.
docs.photoDesc: Recent official color photograph with pure white background. Standard specifications from source: 35x45 mm size, head height 31-36 mm, with 3-5 mm top margin above head.
docs.photoTip: Practical tip: Balanced lighting without shadows, neutral expression, and avoidance of reflective eyewear.
docs.birthCertDesc: Required by specific scholarships to confirm birth date, birthplace, age, and nationality (especially in undergraduate tracks and certain regional requirements).
docs.birthCertTip: Practical tip: Certified sworn translation with authentication from Ministry of Foreign Affairs and target embassy if specified.
docs.gradCertDesc: High school diploma for Bachelors, Bachelor degree for Masters, or Master degree for PhD. Requires authentication from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and education ministries.
docs.gradCertTip: For graduating students: Most scholarships permit provisional application with an expected graduation certificate and completed semester transcripts.
docs.transcriptDesc: Comprehensive breakdown of all subjects, credit hours, grades, and cumulative GPA across all academic semesters. Attested by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and relevant authority.
docs.transcriptTip: Practical tip: Include an official grading scale legend showing percentage conversion brackets for fair international academic assessment.
docs.recommendationsDesc: Formal letters from university professors or supervisors who taught you directly. Most international programs require 2-3 letters evaluating academic performance and research potential.
docs.recommendationsTip: Practical tip: Must be printed on official university letterhead, signed, stamped, and include the referee institutional email address.
docs.cvDesc: Structured academic CV (such as Europass format or standard academic layout) detailing educational background, research, technical skills, projects, and honors concisely.
docs.cvTip: Practical tip: Zero typos, clean formatting, highlighting achievements directly aligned with your target program.
docs.motivationDesc: The single most decisive application document. Articulates your academic background, rationale for program and university selection, future career goals, and intended community impact.
docs.motivationTip: Practical tip: Never copy online templates. Authenticity, tailored reasoning, and a compelling personal narrative drive selection success.
docs.languageDesc: Requirements vary significantly across programs (e.g., IELTS, TOEFL iBT, Duolingo). Some awards waive test scores if previous study was English-taught (MOI certificate) or include preparatory language years.
docs.languageTip: Practical tip: Review individual criteria; possessing a verified test score broadens eligibility and strengthens competitiveness.
docs.medicalDesc: Official medical fitness certificate from an accredited hospital verifying absence of contagious illnesses, complete with ECG, chest X-ray, and laboratory reports (e.g., CSC China format).
docs.medicalValidityNote: Validity Alert: Medical examination certificates typically remain valid for only 6 months. It is strongly advised to schedule this within the active application window.
docs.medicalTip: Practical tip: Ensure official hospital stamps, physician signature, and stamped applicant photograph on the final report.
docs.policeTitle: 11. Certificate of Good Conduct / Police Clearance
docs.policeDesc: Official criminal record clearance certificate issued by forensic evidence or interior department, required by certain countries for student visa clearance and scholarship enrollment.
docs.policeValidityNote: Validity Alert: Police clearance validity is typically 3 to 6 months only; obtain within or close to the active application window.
docs.policeTip: Practical tip: Translate and attest through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs if required in the host nation language.
docs.researchPlanDesc: Rigorous research plan required for research Masters and PhD degrees, defining study title, problem statement, research questions, methodology, and key literature citations.
docs.researchPlanTip: Practical tip: Discuss with academic advisors prior to submission, aligning scope with departmental faculty research interests.

tips.title: Golden Tips to Boost Acceptance Chances
tips.tip1Desc: Review committees evaluate thousands of submissions and spot generic templates immediately. Speak with authentic voice.
tips.tip2Desc: Tailoring 3 high-quality applications to specific programs is vastly more effective than blasting 20 generic submissions.
tips.tip3Desc: Grammar and typographical errors signal lack of care. Have a peer or academic advisor proofread your letters.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.q1: Are IELTS / TOEFL test scores mandatory for all opportunities?
faq.a1: Not universally. Many universities accept an official English Proficiency Certificate if your prior degree was instructed in English. Check each institution's specific language policy.
faq.q2: What is the difference between full and partial funding?
faq.a2: Full funding typically covers tuition fees, a living stipend, travel allowances, and health insurance. Partial funding usually waives a portion of tuition only.
faq.q3: Can I apply before receiving my final graduation diploma?
faq.a3: Yes! Most degree programs allow final-year students to apply by submitting cumulative transcripts up to the latest completed semester alongside an expected graduation letter.
faq.q4: How far in advance should I start preparing my application?
faq.a4: Starting 2 to 3 months prior to the closing deadline is strongly recommended to gather recommendations, draft personal essays, and legalize documents without stress.

boosters.title: Profile Boosters & Final Quality Checklist
boosters.subtitle: High-impact value additions that distinguish your application from thousands of global applicants:
boosters.satTitle: Standardized International Test Scores (SAT / ACT / GRE / GMAT)
boosters.satDesc: Strong standardized test scores (SAT for undergraduates, GRE/GMAT for postgraduates) substantially boost admission priority and merit ranking even when optional.
boosters.volunteeringDesc: Documented volunteer leadership and social service play a pivotal role in illustrating proactive character and leadership commitment to selection committees.
boosters.coursesDesc: Completing verified online courses and micro-credentials (Coursera, edX, etc.) demonstrates active self-directed learning and continuous skill development.
boosters.reviewTitle: Comprehensive Document Verification & Official Link Access
boosters.reviewDesc: Confirm exact English name concordance across all certificates, verify valid remaining timeframes, and proceed directly to the verified official portal for confident submission.
